chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Dawud al-Sarmi said:

I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him), saying to him: 'I go out in this direction, and perhaps there is no place where I can pray due to the snow; so what should I do?' He said: 'If it is possible for you not to prostrate on the snow, do not prostrate on it; and if it is not possible for you, then level it and prostrate on it.' And this report does not contradict what has been narrated:
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on prostrating on snow during prayer if no other surface is available?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith from Imam al-Rida (AS) illustrates the principle of *al-ikhraj min al-darar* (removal of hardship) in ritual purity, allowing for flexibility when snow interferes with direct prostration. The Imam’s instruction to level the snow if necessary underscores the Shia juristic view that the earth remains a valid place of prostration (*sajd*) provided it is cleared of impurities and distinct from the ground, prioritizing the validity of the prayer over rigid physical conditions.
